body: Not that I'm aware of, the validation rules I pasted in are the only ones that should have any effect.
Ok. I'll try reproducing the issue in the context of an application as the data you've provided is considered 'valid' as far as a unit test is concerned.

I tried setting up something similar in a local testing application and the end_time field was marshalled correctly. Also in your original code sample the `start_time` field has a similiar input definition, and validation rule however that input was marshalled correctly.

Given that you have one working field with a 12 hour format, I recommend you figure out what is different between start_time and end_time and go from there.

I'm not sure why you weren't able to reproduce the issue, but I've reproduced it myself using a barebones  fresh project. I've included instructions below to reproduce the issue, as well as the results of my investigation of the bug:

# Steps to reproduce

## 1. Create database we'll use in our CakePHP project using script below:

``` sql
DROP DATABASE meridian_db;
CREATE DATABASE meridian_db;
USE meridian_db;

CREATE TABLE time_sheets (
    id INT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    start_time DATETIME NOT NULL,
    end_time DATETIME NOT NULL,
    rate INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
    notes TEXT
);
```

## 2. Use composer to create the CakePHP project

Command is: php composer.phar create-project --prefer-dist cakephp/app [app_name]

## 3. Bake all files necessary to have a basic CRUD application

Command is: bin/cake bake all time_sheets

## 4. Insert proper DB credentials in [app_name]/config/app.php 

## 5. Change add/edit view input fields to 12 hour format. Something like this:

``` php
echo $this->Form->input('start_time', ['type' => 'datetime', 
   'interval' => 5,
   'minYear' => date("Y") - 1,
   'maxYear' => date("Y"),
   'timeFormat' => 12,
   'label' => "Start Date and Time"]);
echo $this->Form->input('end_time', ['type' => 'datetime', 
   'interval' => 5,
   'minYear' => date("Y") - 1,
   'maxYear' => date("Y"),
   'timeFormat' => 12,
   'label' => "End Date and Time"]);
```

## 6. Navigate a browser to [yourprojecturl]/time_sheets/add

## 7. Populate start and end time fields with todays date, and 12:10pm and 12:50pm, respectively. Populate other fields however you like.

## 8. Click submit, and observe that the times are both marked as invalid.

# My investigation results

So I spent some time debugging and have discovered the source of the bug, which seems to be in CakePHP core (specifically, Validation.php). 

The reason your test case passes is because the values in the data array containing time information are stored as strings, and not ints. See this screenshot:

![screenshot from 2015-09-24 16 32 54](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1485718/10151511/49d00244-6616-11e5-826d-65bbf282c2be.png)

And due to the way the validation check works in Validation.php, arrays of ints will pass where arrays of strings will not. See for yourself with the tests below, the first will pass and the latter will fail:

``` php
$date = ['year' => 2015, 'month' => 9, 'day' => 21, 'hour' => 12, 'minute' => 30, 'meridian' => 'pm'];
        $this->assertTrue(Validation::datetime($date));

$date = ['year' => '2015', 'month' => '09', 'day' => '21', 'hour' => '12', 'minute' => '30', 'meridian' => 'pm'];
        $this->assertTrue(Validation::datetime($date));
```

I've narrowed the problem down to a strange bit of code in Validation.php (around line 1184 in the version I cloned using the reproduction instructions above, the function in question is '_getDateString()') that will convert a string type hour equalling 12 to 24, which is then marked as an invalid time by a regular expression comparison farther down the line in the validation process. I did all this using xdebug, which was very handy. 

I tried fixing the bug myself, but ended up with more problems than I started with. So hopefully the information I've provided here can be helpful to you guys.
Thanks for the detailed steps @JayWalker512 I will take another look.
